functions.name: readSkeletonData_boneTimelines

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_boneTimelines(Json* bonesJson, Json* animationJson, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw, void* parser_raw)
abi.bonesJson: the Json value of the animation's "bones" key (parent spill [sp+0x30] written at 0x28d328); the block reads it at 0x28d640 and then OVERWRITES that slot with the "time" literal at 0x28d694, so the C keeps it in a parameter
abi.animationJson: the CURRENT animation node, parent spill [sp+0x1c] (written at 0x28d2c8, advanced at 0x28e790..0x28e798). E2 passes it to setError; E3 passes 0
abi.return: 1 = fall through to the ik block at 0x28d840; 0 = left through E2/E3, the parent then returns NULL at 0x28bdcc

functions.semantics: if bonesJson == NULL (0x28d640..0x28d648) or bonesJson->child == NULL (0x28d64c..0x28d658) return 1. Five key pointers are materialised once (0x28d65c..0x28d694): "rotate" -> [sp+0x3c], "scale" -> [sp+0x40], "translate" -> [sp+0x48], "shear" -> [sp+0x54], "time" -> [sp+0x30]. Loop over bone nodes: boneIndex = spSkeletonData_findBoneIndex(data, boneNode->name) (0x28d698..0x28d6a0); -1 (0x28d6a4 cmn r0,#1) -> E2; timelineNode = boneNode->child, NULL -> next bone. Per timeline node: type = timelineNode->name (+0x1c) and a strcmp chain rotate (0x28d6cc) / scale (0x28d6e0) / translate (0x28d6f4) / shear (0x28d708); no match -> E3 (0x28d71c). Branch priority rotate -> translate -> scale -> shear. Back edges: 0x28d824 timelineNode = timelineNode->next, 0x28d834 boneNode = boneNode->next (r6 restored from [sp+0x58] because B10 clobbers it).

time.note: stored to [sp+0x30], overwriting the bones-node spill

bone_index_source.finding: NOT a pointer scan and NOT spSkeletonData_findBone (0x28afbc, returns a pointer). The block calls the distinct .dynsym symbol spSkeletonData_findBoneIndex at 0x28b018 (bl at 0x28d6a0, word 0xebfff65c) and compares the result with -1 (0x28d6a4 cmn r0,#1).
bone_index_source.callee_shape: 0x28b018..0x28b06c, 88 B / 21 insns: count = [data+0x10]; signed <= 0 -> -1; table = [data+0x14]; strcmp([table[i]+4], name) == 0 -> return i (FIRST match); loop while i != count; miss -> -1 (0x28b068 mvn r0,#0)
bone_index_source.symbol_boundary: spSkeletonData_findBone (0x28afbc, 92 B) ends exactly at 0x28b018; the two symbols are adjacent, never interchangeable
bone_index_source.recovered_here: the callee body is translated in this module because no existing module owns it (c/skeleton_find covers findBone/findSlotIndex/findSkin only)
bone_index_source.divergence_from_census: census §7 item 6 describes the IK family's in-block pointer scan (data->ikConstraints at +0x3c/+0x40). The bones family does NOT do that: it calls findBoneIndex. B7's pattern must not be copied here.

quirks: the spill slot [sp+0x30] is reused: it holds the bones node on entry and the "time" literal afterwards (0x28d694), so the loop cannot re-read the parent object
the bone node spill at [sp+0x58] is written only when the bone has timeline children (0x28d6b8 strne): B10 uses r6 as a scratch key register
the 0x28d730..0x28d73c fall-through into B6b (s16 = 1.0, r4 = 0) is unreachable in the original: every matching type has already branched
the original performs all four strcmps before branching; the C if-chain is equivalent because the four literals are distinct

functions.name: readSkeletonData_boneXYTimeline

abi.signature: void readSkeletonData_boneXYTimeline(Json* timelineJson, void* animation_raw, int boneIndex, float coordScale, void* timeline_raw)
abi.coordScale: s16. translate: parser->scale read with `ldr r2,[sp,#0x20]; vldr s16,[r2]` at 0x28da58/0x28da5c (spSkeletonJson+0x00 is the uint32 binary32 scale word). scale: 1.0 forced at 0x28db48. shear: 1.0 forced at 0x28dbb8.
calls: spTranslateTimeline_setFrame(t, i, time, x*s16, s16*y) -> 0x282ad4 (synthetic boundary) 0x28d7c0

functions.semantics: frame = timelineJson->child (0x28d740); timeline->boneIndex (+0x14) = boneIndex (0x28d744); no frames -> tail (0x28d74c). Frame loop head 0x28d768 with frameIndex = 0 set at 0x28d754: time, x, y through Json_getFloat; s17 = x*s16 (0x28d79c), s15 = s16*y (0x28d7b8); setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, x*s16, y*s16) with x in r3 and y at [sp]; then readCurve(frame, timeline, frameIndex); frame = frame->next; ++frameIndex.
functions.tail: 0x28d7e4..0x28d820: declared = Json+0x0c; wordIndex = (declared-1)*3 (`sub r2,r2,#1` then `add r2,r2,r2,lsl#1`); animation->timelineCount = count+1; timelines[count] = timeline; last = frames[wordIndex] (frames at +0x10, `add r3,r3,r2,lsl#2`); animation->duration = (duration > last) ? duration : last.
functions.setframe_abi: spTranslateTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, x, y): r0=timeline, r1=frameIndex, r2=time, r3=x, [sp]=y (softfp; the original vmov r3,s17 and vstr s15,[sp]). One call site (0x28d7c0) serves translate, scale AND shear: spScaleTimeline_setFrame (0x282b1c) and spShearTimeline_setFrame (0x282b38) are 4-byte `b spTranslateTimeline_setFrame` thunks.
functions.frame_stride: 3 floats per frame: frames[i*3+0]=time, [+1]=x, [+2]=y (real setter 0x282ad4: 0x282ae8 `add r1,r0,r1,lsl#2` after 0x282ad4 `add r1,r1,r1,lsl#1`). The tail reads frames[3*(declared-1)].
quirks: the frame loop is driven by the child list, while the tail indexes frames[3*(declared-1)]; a short child list leaves never-written slots, declared == 0 reads frames[0xFFFFFFFD]
x is evaluated before y and multiplied as x*s16, y as s16*y (operand order preserved because VFP NaN quieting depends on it)
the timeline record's +0x14 is written before the frame==NULL test (0x28d744 precedes 0x28d748)

functions.name: readSkeletonData_boneRotateTimeline

abi.signature: void readSkeletonData_boneRotateTimeline(Json* timelineJson, void* animation_raw, int boneIndex)

functions.semantics: timeline = spRotateTimeline_create(timelineJson->unk_0c) (0x28da74/0x28da78); frame = timelineJson->child (0x28da7c); timeline->boneIndex (+0x14) = boneIndex (0x28da88); no frames -> tail. Frame loop head 0x28daa8 with the index in r9: time = Json_getFloat(frame,"time",0), angle = Json_getFloat(frame,"angle",0); spRotateTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, angle); readCurve(frame, timeline, frameIndex); frame = frame->next; ++frameIndex.
functions.frame_index_source: r9 arrives as 0 from the dispatch: 0x28d6d0 `subs r9,r0,#0` writes the rotate strcmp result into r9 and the branch at 0x28d6d4 is taken only when it is 0. B10 has no explicit clear.
functions.tail: 0x28db0c..0x28db40: count = animation->timelineCount; duration; timelines = animation->timelines; declared = Json+0x0c; timelineCount = count+1; timelines[count] = timeline; last = frames[declared*2-2] (`add r3,r3,r2,lsl#3` then `vldr s15,[r3,#-8]`); duration = (duration > last) ? duration : last; b 0x28d824.
functions.setframe_abi: spRotateTimeline_setFrame(timeline, frameIndex, time, angle): r0=timeline, r1=frameIndex, r2=time, r3=angle.
functions.frame_stride: 2 floats per frame: frames[i*2+0]=time, [+1]=angle (real setter 0x282aac `add r1,r0,r1,lsl#3`, stores at [r1] and [r1,#4]). The tail reads frames[2*(declared-1)] via frames[declared*2] with a -8 byte displacement.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_boneNotFound

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_boneNotFound(Json* boneNode, Json* animationJson, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw, void* parser_raw)
calls: _spSkeletonJson_setError(parser, animationJson, "Bone not found: ", boneNode->name) -> 0x28b784 (real; console vcall + line-90 copy) 0x28db80

functions.semantics: type text = boneNode->name (+0x1c, 0x28db78). spAnimation_dispose(animation) FIRST (0x28db68), then setError (0x28db6c..0x28db80), then the shared error tail at 0x28da44: spSkeletonData_dispose(data) and return 0 (parent b 0x28bdcc).

set_error_arguments.json: r1 = [sp+0x1c] (0x28db74) = the CURRENT ANIMATION JSON NODE, NOT NULL and NOT the root. setError therefore Json_disposes that node and its siblings; the root tree survives.

quirks: the json argument is the animation node, so this error path disposes part of the JSON tree — unlike E1 (r1 = 0, 0x28da38) and E3 (r4 = 0)
the animation is disposed BEFORE the error text is formatted; the half-built skeleton data AFTER it
the message copy is a line-90 SkeletonJson.c allocation through _malloc

set_error_arguments.json: r1 = r4 (0x28db9c `mov r1,r4`). r4 is the OR of the four strcmp match flags (`orr r4,r9,r5` 0x28d70c, `orrs r4,r0,r4` 0x28d718) and the E3 branch is taken only when that OR is zero, so the argument is exactly NULL: the tree is NOT disposed.
set_error_arguments.message: "Invalid timeline type for a bone: " @0x357eec (pool 0x28ea94, add 0x28dba8)

the offending text is the timeline node's JSON member key, not a string value

the loop condition is i != count, not i < count (guarded by the count > 0 test)

open: The declared frame count is the word at Json+0x0c; the loop follows the child list. declared == 0 makes the tails read frames[-1] (xy) / frames[-2] (rotate) and the creators receive 0; the fixture never drives a zero declared count, so the original's behaviour there is not asserted.
A frame without an "x"/"y"/"angle"/"time" key silently receives 0.0f from Json_getFloat; that is real accessor behaviour, not a guard of this family.
A bone node whose name is NULL (or a missing "bones" member on a bone) reaches spSkeletonData_findBoneIndex and strcmp(NULL); the original has no guard.

Why the original reuses spTranslateTimeline_setFrame for scale/shear instead of calling their own 4-byte thunks cannot be derived from the instruction stream; the module mirrors the observed call target and the checker pins both thunks.

The exact semantics of the four timeline-type constants passed to _spCurveTimeline_init (0x282a48/0x282a4c: r1 = 1/2/0/3 and r2 = frameStep) belong to the unrecovered creators; the fixture's +0x00 type word is a tag, not the original enum value.

E2 disposes the animation JSON node (r1 = [sp+0x1c]); Json_dispose also walks that node's siblings, so on this error path the remaining animation members are freed as well. That follows from the real Json_dispose body, but the original's observable behaviour after the returning NULL is not exercised.
spSkeletonData_findBoneIndex is recovered in this module as a stand-in; if c/skeleton_find later owns it, this copy must be removed.
No skeleton JSON asset exists in this tree, so how many bone timelines the shipped data actually uses is unknown.
